justification: Verdict INVALID. The designated flawed_step/counterexample target line 0024 (base case of Lemma 1's induction on SHORTEST path length), not the ground-truth defect (the cyclic => multiple reductions direction, refuted by the 2-cycle a<->b whose transitive reduction is unique). The line-0024 flaw is genuine and I checked it concretely: with G = {u->v, u->w, w->v}, G is acyclic, GT = {(u,v),(u,w),(w,v)}, and the shortest u->v path has length 1, yet the intermediate w satisfies (u,w),(w,v) in GT, so (u,v) is NOT in R under the line-0015 definition. The base-case assertion 'no intermediate vertex w exists, so (u,v) in R' is therefore false. The second witness G' = {u->v, u->a, a->b, b->w, w->v} also checks out: shortest(u,v)=1 while shortest(u,w)=3, so the inductive step's claim that both sub-paths are strictly shorter than k fails; the induction genuinely must be on longest path length. So this is a real, independently verified defect distinct from the ground truth. Note (does not change the grade): the reasoning_summary parenthetically states the ground-truth flaw with the exact ground-truth witness ('for a bare 2-cycle v1<->v2 ... the transitive reduction is in fact unique, so the k=2 case is not handled'), but explicitly flags it as 'noted but not relied on' and it does not appear in flawed_step or counterexample; a lenient reading could call this CAUGHT_MATCHING.
